verdict.rationale: Context.dev documents Scrape returning HTML. Its browser actions (click, wait, scroll before Scrape captures a page) and its screenshot feature, which renders a URL, imply a real browser rendering step. However, the docs never explicitly state that the HTML output is the fully JavaScript-rendered DOM of a single-page application. missing for 10: explicit documentation that scraped HTML reflects client-side JS execution, SPA-specific rendering controls or examples, and independent hands-on corroboration on JS-heavy sites.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render JavaScript-heavy single-page applications and get the fully rendered HTML

citations.quote: Scrape a page into Markdown, HTML, a screenshot, images, or CSS-selected fields in one request.
Click, scroll, or wait before Scrape captures a page, then verify the result from the captured output.
Render an exact URL or a resolved site page and return a viewport, full-page, or offset PNG capture.
